Tafsir of Surah Luqman

All of it is Meccan except three verses, which we will indicate when we reach them, and Allah knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif, Lam, Meem. These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾. That is: the one made firm (muhkam) concerning the lawful and the unlawful, and the mention of the rulings. It is also said: [it is firm] concerning the promise and the warning, and the reward and the punishment. Some of them said: "al-Hakim" (the Wise) is the one that clarifies wisdom, like the wise one (hakim) who speaks with wisdom.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 3:

And His words: ﴿A guidance and a mercy﴾. Most readers recited it with the accusative (naṣb), and al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjāj) said: "It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl)." Ḥamzah recited "hudan wa raḥmah" (with the nominative), meaning: "It is guidance and mercy." Its meaning is: a clarification (bayān) from misguidance, and a mercy from punishment.

And His words: ﴿for the good-doers﴾, meaning: for the Muslims, for the Muslim is a good-doer to himself. It has been authentically reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about excellence (iḥsān), and he said: "That you worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you." It is also said: the good-doer (al-muḥsin) is the one who loves for people what he loves for himself.
And His saying: ﴿Those who establish prayer and give zakat, and they are certain of the Hereafter﴾ — we have already explained it.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾, and His saying: ﴿And those are the successful ones﴾. That is, the felicitous (al-su'ada'), and it is said: the saved (al-najun). And it is said: they are those who attained what they hoped for and were delivered from what they fled from.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 6:

Concerning His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among people is one who purchases idle talk﴾, al-Kalbi and Muqatil mentioned that the verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah. He used to go to al-Hirah and buy the stories of the non-Arabs (al-'Ajam). Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) recited the Qur'an, he would stand up and say: "O people, Muhammad relates to you about 'Ad and Thamud, and I relate to you about Rustam, Isfandiyar and the Persians (al-'Ajam). So I have better stories than him." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse concerning him.

Abu Umamah al-Bahili narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The teaching of singing-girls is forbidden, and selling them and buying them is forbidden, and their price is forbidden." Then he recited His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among people is one who purchases idle talk﴾, and said: "No man raises his voice with singing except that two devils come, one sits upon his right shoulder and the other upon his left shoulder, and they strike their feet upon his back and chest until he is the one who falls silent."

From Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and most of the exegetes, that the verse was revealed concerning singing (al-ghina'). Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to swear to this. From Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, who said: "They used to say that singing causes hypocrisy to grow in the heart." Ibrahim said: "They used to block the mouths of the alleys and tear the tambourines." From al-Dahhak, who said: ﴿And among people is one who purchases idle talk﴾ is associating partners with Allah. From Ibn Jurayj: it is the drum. In the reports with chains (al-akhbar al-musnadah) it is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is the musical instruments (al-ma'azif) and the singing-girls (al-qayan)." From Sahl ibn Abdullah al-Tustari, who said: idle talk is disputation about the religion and plunging into falsehood.

As for His saying: ﴿so that he may mislead [others] from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., the religion of Allah. It was also read as "liyudilla 'an sabili Allah" with a fatha on the ya' (yaa). So His saying ﴿liyudilla﴾ means: so that he may mislead others.

And His saying ﴿liyudilla﴾ means: so that he may himself come to be in error.

And His saying ﴿without knowledge and takes it in mockery﴾ means: he takes the signs of Allah in mockery. It is also said: he takes the way of Allah in mockery. The sabil (way) is mentioned both as masculine and feminine. The poet said:

(Men wish that I would die, and if I die, / then that is a path in which I am not unique.)

As for His saying: ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾, its meaning is apparent, and we have explained it before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 7:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly, as though he had not heard them﴾, meaning: as though he had not heard the verses.

And His words: ﴿as though there were deafness in his ears﴾, meaning: deafness. He made him like this because he did not benefit from what he heard, so he became like one who is deaf. The waqr (heaviness) is the weight in the ear.

And His words: ﴿so give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾, meaning: painful (mu'lim), and the meaning of mu'lim is: that which causes pain.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verses 8–9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have gardens of bliss, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true.﴾ Its meaning: remaining in the Garden, as Allah has promised.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Al-'Aziz (the Mighty) is the One who takes vengeance on His enemies, and al-Hakim (the Wise) is the One who is correct in the management of His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verses 8–9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have gardens of bliss, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true.﴾ Its meaning: remaining in the Garden, as Allah has promised.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Al-'Aziz (the Mighty) is the One who takes vengeance on His enemies, and al-Hakim (the Wise) is the One who is correct in the management of His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars﴾, meaning: without pillars that you can see. The second meaning: without pillars that you see; but there are pillars that you do not see, and that pillar is the power of God, may He be exalted. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease [to move]﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains﴾, meaning: fixed mountains. Al-Suddi mentioned that God, may He be exalted, created the earth and it began to tilt, so the angels said: "O our Lord, no one can settle upon the back of this earth." So in the morning God had fixed it with mountains. They said: "O our Lord, have You created anything stronger than the mountains?" He said: "Yes; iron." They said: "O our Lord, have You created anything stronger than iron?" He said: "Yes; fire." They said: "Have You created anything stronger than fire?" He said: "Yes; water." They said: "Have You created anything stronger than water?" He said: "Yes; wind." They said: "Have You created anything stronger than wind?" He said: "Yes; the son of Adam." Some have traced this report to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and at the end of the report: "The son of Adam gives charity and conceals his charity, so that his left hand does not know what his right hand has given; he is stronger than all of them."

And His saying: ﴿lest it should sway with you﴾, meaning: lest it sway with you. It is said: "out of dislike that it should sway with you." Al-Mayd means al-mayl (inclination, swaying).

And His saying: ﴿And He spread therein every kind of moving creature﴾, meaning: He scattered therein every kind of moving creature. Al-Dabbah (moving creature) is every living being that crawls upon the earth.

And His saying: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky, and We caused to grow therein every noble kind of pair﴾, meaning: every good kind.

The Almighty's statement: ﴿This is the creation of God; so show me what those beside Him have created.﴾ That is, those who worship other than Him, namely the idols. It has been narrated from some of the early pious predecessors (al-salaf) that he said: "I never saw anything without seeing God in it." Some of them attributed this to Amir ibn Abd Qays, who is Amir ibn Abd Allah. He comes right after Uways al-Qarani among the ascetics of the Successors (al-tabi'in), and he is among the foremost ascetics of the Successors, may God be pleased with them all. (﴿11)

And indeed We gave Luqman wisdom, [saying], "Be grateful to God. And whoever is grateful, he is grateful only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever disbelieves..." Eight men: the first of them is Uways, then Amir ibn Abd Qays, then Harim ibn Hayyan, then Abu Muslim al-Khawlani, then al-Aswad, then Masruq ibn al-Ajda', then al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, then al-Hasan.

As for His statement: ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error.﴾ That is, in obvious mistake.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 31, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾. The scholars differed concerning Luqman: was he a prophet or not a prophet? The majority of the people of knowledge held that he was not a prophet.

Al-Sha'bi (a major Successor scholar) and Ikrimah (a student of Ibn 'Abbas) said that he was a prophet. It is reported from some of them that Allah gave him the choice between prophethood and wisdom, and he chose wisdom. He slept a sleep, and wisdom was poured upon his tongue, so he woke up speaking with wisdom. Some of them also mentioned that he was asked: "Why did you choose wisdom over prophethood?" He said: "I feared that I would be too weak for it. Had Allah given it to me from the start without informing me, He would have helped me with it; but when He gave me the choice, I feared weakness."

It is reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that he said: "Luqman was a black slave from the blacks of Egypt." And from another he said: "He was an Abyssinian slave, thick-lipped, with cracked feet." It is related that a black slave asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab about a matter and he answered him, then said to him: "Let not your blackness grieve you, for before you there were three blacks who were among the best of people: Luqman the Wise, Bilal the muezzin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Mihja', the freed slave of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he was the first martyr in Islam; he was martyred on the day of Badr."

They differed concerning Luqman's occupation. Some said he was a tailor, some said he was a carpenter, and some said he was a shepherd. It is related that someone met him while he was speaking wisdom and said: "Are you not so-and-so the shepherd? By what did you reach what you have reached?" He said: "By truthfulness of speech, fulfilling trusts, and leaving what does not concern me."

Among his transmitted wise sayings: his master gave him a sheep and said: "Slaughter it and bring me the two best pieces of it." So he brought its tongue and its heart. His master asked him about this, and he said: "There is nothing better than these two when they are good, and nothing more wicked than these two when they are corrupt." It is also reported from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: "Luqman spoke twelve thousand chapters of wisdom, which people have incorporated into their speech and their admonitions."

The wisdom mentioned in this verse means understanding and correctness in speech. It is also said: complete intellect.

His saying: ﴿That give thanks to Allah﴾, i.e., for His blessings.

His saying: ﴿And whoever gives thanks, he gives thanks only for himself﴾, i.e., the benefit of gratitude returns to him.

His saying: ﴿And whoever is ungrateful, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., Free of need from His creation, Praiseworthy in His actions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 13:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when Luqman said to his son while he was admonishing him﴾. It is said: the name of his son was Mashkam; it is also said: An'am; and it was said: other than that.

And His words: ﴿O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is a great wrong﴾. That is: do not equate anyone with Allah in lordship (rububiyyah).

And His words: ﴿Indeed, association [with Him] is a great wrong﴾. Zulm (wrongdoing, injustice) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. Whoever associates someone with Allah has placed a thing in other than its proper place.

"And We have enjoined upon man (care) for his parents. His mother bore him in weakness upon weakness."

Literally: weakness upon weakness, i.e., weakness upon weakness. It is also said: hardship upon hardship. Al-Zajjaj said: When a woman conceives, weakness and hardship follow one another for her. It is also said: the pregnancy is a weakness, the labour pains are a weakness, and the delivery is a weakness.

And His saying: ﴿And his weaning is in two years﴾ means: his weaning is within two years, and the two years are the end of the period of weaning.

And His saying: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents﴾. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: Whoever prays the five prayers at their appointed times has given thanks to Allah the Exalted, and whoever seeks forgiveness for his parents after every prayer has given thanks to his parents.

And His saying: ﴿To Me is the destination﴾ means: to Me is the return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge﴾. The meaning of this verse has already been explained, and we mentioned that it was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Some of them said: the verse is general, applying to everyone.

His saying: ﴿So do not obey them﴾, meaning: do not obey them in associating others with Me and in disobeying Me.

His saying: ﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness﴾, meaning: keep company with them in this world with goodness and kinship, which is the kindness (ma'ruf), without obeying them in disobedience to Me.

His saying: ﴿And follow the way of those who turn back to Me in repentance﴾. Most of the commentators said that this refers to Muhammad (ﷺ).

His saying: ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾. The meaning is clear.

It is narrated from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And follow the way of those who turn back to Me in repentance﴾, that what is meant by it is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn 'Abbas said: When Abu Bakr embraced Islam, 'Uthman, Talha, al-Zubayr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf came to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them all, and they said: "O Abu Bakr, has this man truly been in the right, and have you believed in him?" He said: "Yes, he is truthful, so believe in him." He brought them to the Prophet (ﷺ) until they embraced Islam. These people have the precedence of Islam, and they embraced Islam through the guidance of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them. And Allah, may He be exalted, revealed concerning Abu Bakr: ﴿And follow the way of those who turn back to Me in repentance﴾.

His saying: ﴿Anab﴾ means "turned back" to Me, and according to this view it refers to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

"The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O my son, indeed it, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed﴾. If it is said: the words "innahā" (indeed it) here are a pronoun (kināya), and a pronoun must have something it refers to; so what is the referent? The answer to this: it is related that Luqman's son said: "O father, what do you think if something falls into the maqal (the central part, i.e. the middle) of the sea, will Allah the Exalted know its place?" He said: "O my son, indeed it, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed," meaning: if a grain of this weight falls into this sea, Allah the Exalted knows its place. Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that Luqman threw a mustard seed into the width of the river Yarmuk, sat on its bank and extended his hand, and a fly dived, took the mustard seed and placed it on his palm.

There is another view regarding the verse: that the words of Allah the Exalted "innahā in takun" refer to the wrongdoing (khati'a), meaning: if the wrongdoing is like the weight of a mustard seed, Allah the Exalted will bring it on the Day of Resurrection, i.e., He will recompense you for it. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the meaning of the verse is the encompassing of things, small and great.

And His words: ﴿so it would be in a rock﴾, i.e., in a mountain. Al-Suddi said: it is the rock upon which the seven earths rest, and it is a green rock, from which the greenness of the sky comes.

And His words: ﴿or in the heavens or in the earth; Allah will bring it forth﴾.

And His words: ﴿Indeed Allah is Subtle, Acquainted﴾. Abu al-Aliyah said: Subtle in extracting the mustard seed, Acquainted with its place. In some tafsirs it is related that this was the last wisdom Luqman spoke, and when he spoke it, his gall bladder burst from its awe, and he died."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 17:

His saying: ﴿O my son, establish prayer and enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong﴾ We have already explained the meaning of "what is good" (al-ma'ruf) and the meaning of "what is wrong" (al-munkar) earlier.

And His saying: ﴿And be patient over what befalls you﴾ That is, over harm (al-adha).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾ That is, of the matters that one is commanded to do and must resolve upon. Huthayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "It is not for the believer to abase himself." It was said: "And how does he abase himself?" He said: "He takes upon himself a trial beyond what he can bear." In this report there is a concession (rukhsah) to abandon enjoining what is good before rulers and oppressors when one fears destruction. And if one enjoins what is good and is killed for it, then he is a martyr (shahid).

It has also been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The best jihad is a word of truth before an oppressive ruler."

It is also narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The master of the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection is Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, then a man who stood before a ruler, fearing him and hoping for him, and enjoined him to what is good or forbade him from what is wrong, so he was killed for that."

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 18:**

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾ means: do not turn away from them out of arrogance. *Al-sa'r* (a twisting or turning of the neck, i.e. aversion) is *al-mayl* (inclining away). In some reports it is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There will come upon the people a time when none will remain except one who is *asy'ar*," meaning: one who does not claim the religion. It is also said that His statement ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾ prohibits *al-tashaddu'* (affected, pompous speech) in speech. And on the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, he said: "Let the rich and the poor be equal in your sight."

His statement: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾ means: do not walk upon the earth in self-admiring pride.

His statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love every self-deluded boaster﴾ means: one who is self-deluded toward the earth, boasting of the worldly life.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And be moderate in your pace﴾ means: hasten in your walking. It is also said its meaning is: be moderate in your pace, i.e., do not hasten in your walking. And in some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "Hastening in walking takes away the light of the face."

And His saying: ﴿And lower your voice﴾ means: do not raise it. The meaning of "lower" (ighdud) is: reduce. It is said: "So-and-so lowered (ghadda) so-and-so," meaning he diminished his right.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the most hideous of voices is the braying of donkeys﴾ means: the most repugnant of voices is the voice of donkeys. It is said: "So-and-so came to me with a disapproving (munkar) face," meaning an ugly one. If someone asks: Why did He make the donkey's voice the most ugly of voices? The answer: He made it the most ugly of voices because its beginning is zafir (exhaling groan) and its end is shahiq (inhaling groan), and zafir and shahiq are the voices of the people of the Fire. It is reported from Sufyan al-Thawri that he said: "Everything glorifies (God) except the donkey; therefore its voice was made the most ugly of voices."

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to compete in loudness of voice, saying: "Whoever has the louder voice is more honored with God." They would raise their voices to the utmost possible. So God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse, and its meaning is: honor does not lie in loudness of voice; for if loudness were the measure, the donkey would be more honored than all. It is also reported from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sadiq that he said regarding His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the most hideous of voices is the braying of donkeys﴾: it is the ugly, repugnant sneeze.

Among the wise sayings of Luqman, apart from what we have mentioned, is what is related: he said, "No wealth is like health of the body, and no delight is like contentment of the soul." Also among his wisdom: he said, "A father's discipline of his child is like fertilizer for the crop."

Ikrimah related that Luqman entered upon Dawud, peace be upon him, while he was making a coat of mail, and he did not know what he was making, so he wanted to ask him, but his wisdom prevented him from it. When Dawud finished the coat of mail and wore it, he said: "Yes, it is a battle garment." Luqman said: "Silence is wisdom, and few are those who practise it."

Ikrimah also related that the master of Luqman wagered a group of people that he could drink the sea water while intoxicated. He called Luqman and said: "For such a day I have been keeping you," and told him the story. He said: "Gather the people with whom you made the wager." So he gathered them, and he said to them: "Hold back the sources of the sea until he drinks the sea water." They said: "How can we hold back the sources of the sea?" He said: "How can he drink the sea water while its sources are not cut off?" So his master was freed from the wager.

Ikrimah also related that Luqman's master had other slaves besides him, and none of them was more contemptible in his eyes than Luqman. He sent them to an orchard of his to bring him fruit. They went and ate the fruit; when they returned, they blamed Luqman, claiming that he was the one who had eaten it. His master believed them because of Luqman's lowly standing in his eyes, and wanted to harm him. Luqman said to his master: "Indeed, the two-tongued and the two-faced will not be honored with God. Give me hot water to drink, and give these slaves hot water to drink." So he gave them to drink; all the other slaves vomited what they had eaten of the fruit, while he vomited plain water. Thus his truthfulness and their lying became known.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Do you not see that God has subjected to you what is in the heavens and what is on the earth?﴾ means: He made them submissive (dhallala).

And His saying: ﴿and has completed for you His blessings﴾ means: He perfected for you and completed His blessings, both outward and inward. Ibn 'Abbas said: the outward blessing is Islam and good character, and the inward blessing is what covers over faults. Some of them said: the outward blessing is verbal affirmation with the tongue, and the inward is belief in the heart. It is also said: the outward blessing is the blessing of this world, and the inward is the blessing of the Hereafter. It was said: the outward blessing is the blessing of bodies, and the inward is the blessing of religions. It is said: the outward blessing is complete provision, and the inward blessing is good character. It is said: the outward blessing is attire and fine adornment, and the inward blessing is what hides and conceals sin. Some of them said: the outward blessing is children, and the inward is intercourse.

And His saying: ﴿And among people is one who disputes about God without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾ was revealed concerning Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and their likes. They used to dispute with the Prophet, with falsehood, about God and His attributes.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather we follow what we found our fathers upon."﴾ The meaning is apparent.

And His saying: ﴿Even though Shaytan (Satan) was calling them to the punishment of the Blaze?﴾ This is an answer to an omitted (elided) part, and the omitted part is: "Would they follow Shaytan," even if Shaytan was calling them to the punishment of the Blaze."

And whoever submits his face to Allah, [while he is good-doing], has indeed grasped the most trustworthy handhold. Its meaning: He who sincerely devotes his religion to Allah. It was also said: he submits himself and his deeds to Allah.

Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Sulamī recited *yusallim* with a shaddah (emphatic doubling). The verb *yusallim* from *taslīm* (surrender), and *yasallim* (with its vowel as read) from *infiyād* (submission).

His saying: "[and he is good-doing], has indeed grasped the most trustworthy handhold" refers to the statement "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: the most trustworthy handhold is the means that leads to the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted. *Al-wuthqā* is the feminine of *al-awthaq* (the most firm). A *ʿahd wathīq* is a firm, strong covenant, and *al-awthaq* means the stronger.

His saying: "And to Allah belongs the outcome of affairs" means: the final end of affairs.

"Let not their disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts. We will give them enjoyment for a little, then We will force them to a severe punishment. And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Praise be to Allah.' But most of them do not know. To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens and the sea, replenished by seven seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise. Your creation and resurrection are not but like that of a single soul."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 23:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you﴾. That is: do not grieve over his disbelief.

And His saying: ﴿To Us is their return﴾. That is: their destination.

And His saying: ﴿Then We will inform them of what they did﴾. That is: We will tell them of what they did.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾. That is: Knowing of what is in the breasts.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿We will let them enjoy themselves briefly﴾. Imta' is enjoying the pleasures of this world and its bounties.

And His saying: ﴿Then We will compel them to a severe punishment﴾. That is: We will force them into a severe punishment.

The word of God Most High: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?", they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah." But most of them do not know.﴾ We have already explained it.

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾. That is: the Free of need from His creation, the Praised in His actions.

The Almighty's words: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens﴾. It is related that the polytheists said: "What Muhammad (ﷺ) brings of speech will come to an end and perish." So God Most High revealed this verse, meaning: even if all the trees of the world and their plants were cut into pens, and the seas became ink, the words of God would not be exhausted, that is, the speech of God and His knowledge.

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, God is Mighty and Wise﴾, we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verses 28–30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul﴾. Its meaning: Your creation is only like the creation of a single soul, and your resurrection is only like the resurrection of a single soul, meaning: in relation to His power.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾: Hearing of the words of the servants, Seeing of their deeds. As for the verse that follows this verse to its end, we have already explained its meaning. And as for the three verses which were revealed in Medina, they are from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if whatever trees upon the earth were pens﴾, to the end of the three verses.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you not see that the ship runs through the sea by the favor of Allah?﴾ Meaning: by the bounty of Allah.

His saying: ﴿That He may show you of His signs﴾ means: of the wonders of His creation and His power.

His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for everyone who is steadfast and grateful﴾ It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Patience is half of faith, gratitude is half of faith, and certainty is the whole of faith." And in some reports: the most beloved of the servants to Allah is the one who is patient at the time of trial, grateful at the time of blessings, and content with the decree.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 32:

His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows (ẓulal)﴾. Ẓulal is the plural of ẓullah, and ẓullah is the mountain.

And his saying: ﴿calling upon Allah, making the religion sincerely His﴾. That is: they made their supplication sincere. It is said in the tafsir that this verse was revealed concerning ʿIkrimah ibn Abi Jahl, when he fled from Makkah on the day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had granted safety to all the people except a few of them, among whom was ʿIkrimah ibn Abi Jahl. So ʿIkrimah fled toward the sea, and a violent wind came upon them. The captain of the ship said: "Be sincere, for nothing will save you except sincerity." It is also narrated that he said to them: "Do not call upon your gods, for your gods will not avail you anything, but call upon Allah alone."

ʿIkrimah said: "I only fled from this. If Allah saves me from this, I will certainly return to Muhammad and place my hand in his hand." Then the wind subsided, ʿIkrimah came out and returned to Makkah, embraced Islam and his Islam was good, and he was martyred on the day of Yarmuk in al-Sham.

And his saying: ﴿So when He brings them safely to the shore, some of them are moderate (muqtaṣid)﴾. That is: he is just in his conduct, in the sense of fulfilling what he promised. Some have said: muqtaṣid means moderate in speech, not extravagant, and among them is one who transgresses.

And his saying: ﴿And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous (khattār), ungrateful one﴾. Khatr is the most extreme treachery.

The poet said:

(For if you had seen Abu ʿUmayr… you would have filled your hands with treachery and deceit.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 33:

The words of God Most High: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son at all, nor will a son avail his father in anything.﴾ That is: no father will suffice to avail his son. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Every person will be concerned with himself."

And His words: ﴿Nor will a child avail his father in anything.﴾ That is: one who will suffice in place of his father in anything.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, the promise of God is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver (al-Gharur) delude you concerning God.﴾ He means: Satan. His deluding of the human being is his adorning of sins for him and his raising in him hopes of forgiveness from God. He expressed this by his adorning sins for him and his raising in him hopes of forgiveness.

In a report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The shrewd one is he who holds himself to account (dana nafsahu) and works for what comes after death (i.e., takes account of himself), and the wicked one is he who follows his desires and wishes (tamanna) for forgiveness from God."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 31, verse 34:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain﴾ – the verse. In the tafsir it is related that a man from the Banu Muharib ibn Khasafa came to the Prophet and said: "O Muhammad, our land has become barren, so when will the rain descend? I have left my wife pregnant, so what will she give birth to? I know what I am doing today, so what will I do tomorrow? Tell me in which land I will die. Tell me when the Hour will come." So Allah the Most High revealed this verse to its end.

We have also related, through the narration of Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The keys of the unseen are five," and he recited this verse to its end. This is a well-known report.

As for His words: ﴿[And He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow] and no soul knows in which land it will die﴾, it is said that its meaning is: "On which foot it will die." For there is no step a person lifts and sets down except that he may die before it. ﴿In which land it will die﴾ means: in what state it will die, of wretchedness or happiness.

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware﴾, its meaning is apparent.
